questions.q: The IP address 130.10.5.2 belongs to which class?
questions.solution: First octet 130 lies in **128-191 = Class B**.

questions.q: **Hot-swappable** means a device can be —
options: Connected or removed while the computer is running
Used only when the PC is switched off
questions.solution: **Hot-swap = plug or unplug with the system running** — no restart. USB is the everyday example.

questions.q: Which shortcut opens the BROWSING HISTORY panel?
questions.solution: **Ctrl+H = History**; Ctrl+J opens the downloads list — the standard trap pair.

questions.q: The World Wide Web was invented in 1989 by:
questions.solution: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the WWW at CERN in 1989 and wrote the first browser. Vint Cerf co-designed TCP/IP; Larry Page co-founded Google.
questions.shortcut: Web = Berners-Lee, 1989, CERN. Internet (1970s TCP/IP) = Cerf and Kahn.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To pay through the nose
options: to pay one's bills on time
to pay far more than the fair price
questions.solution: *Pay through the nose* = to be charged much too much. Example: buying water at an airport. The breathing option is literal.
questions.shortcut: Nose idiom about money = paying too much.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (3).
questions.solution: The librarian collects old newspapers 'for a small archive'. The action an archive needs is **preserve** — keep old copies safe. *Publish* creates new copies, *repair* fixes damage, *translate* changes the language; none means 'store for the future'.
questions.shortcut: Match the verb to the purpose word in the sentence ('for an archive').
questions.passage: The corporation library on Gandhi Road now stays open till eleven at night. The change began when a clerk noticed students reading under the streetlight after closing time. The reading hall, once half (1) ______, is now full by eight o'clock. Regulars say the quiet here has a different (2) ______ from the quiet of their homes, where the television mutters in every room. The librarian has also begun to (3) ______ old newspapers for a small archive that students use to trace how an issue developed. Pleased by the response, the corporation has sanctioned two more fans, and the students (4) ______ full advantage of the extended hours.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: Restaurant = **rest-au-rant**: the 'au' sits between rest and rant. Restaraunt reverses to 'ar'; Restauraunt adds a phantom u.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (3).
questions.solution: The fixed expression is **(keep) away from**: cattle are kept away **from** the shallow edge. 'Away off', 'away at' and 'away beyond' are not the idiom; the sentence already supplies 'away', and 'away' pairs with *from*.
questions.shortcut: away → from. Read the whole phrase around the blank.
questions.passage: The lake behind the sugar mill had become a grey pond that smelled (1) ______ chemicals. Three years ago the villagers formed a committee and decided to set (2) ______ a small fund for desilting the lake bed. Fish returned the following spring. The committee now guards the lake strictly: anyone caught dumping waste must pay a fine, and cattle are kept away (3) ______ the shallow edge by a low stone fence. (4) ______ the committee's records, the lake has not gone dry even once since the desilting.

questions.q: The Rigvedic river **Asikni** is the modern —
questions.solution: **Asikni = Chenab**. Full chain: Vitasta-Jhelum, Asikni-Chenab, Parushni-Ravi, Vipas-Beas, Sutudri-Sutlej.
questions.shortcut: Second in both chains (V-A-P-V-S and J-C-R-B-S) → Chenab.

questions.q: **Servants of India Society** (1905), which trained dedicated public workers, was founded by —
questions.solution: **Gokhale** founded the Servants of India Society in 1905 — he was also Gandhi's acknowledged political guru.

questions.q: The **Arthashastra**, a treatise on statecraft and economy, is attributed to —
questions.solution: The *Arthashastra* is attributed to **Kautilya (Chanakya)**, Chandragupta Maurya's minister; it covers taxation, espionage, diplomacy and administration.

questions.q: **Anaemia** is chiefly caused by the deficiency of —
questions.solution: **Iron** builds the haemoglobin that carries oxygen; low iron → pale, tired, breathless. Vitamin B₁₂ deficiency gives the rarer pernicious anaemia.

questions.q: The mean of the squares of the first 10 natural numbers is:
questions.shortcut: 38.5 = $\frac{77}{2}$. Trap: 55 — the mean of naturals squared wrongly.

questions.q: A train running at 54 km/h crosses a pole in 12 seconds and a platform in 30 seconds. The length of the platform is:
questions.solution: $S = 54 \times \frac{5}{18} = 15$ m/s. Train length $= 15 \times 12 = 180$ m. Platform $= 15 \times 30 - 180 = 270$ m.

questions.q: A 300 m long train crosses a pole in 15 seconds. The speed of the train is:
In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A = 60^\circ$. If $I$ is the incentre of the triangle, then $\angle BIC$ equals:
questions.solution: $\angle BIC = 90^\circ + \frac{A}{2} = 90^\circ + 30^\circ = 120^\circ$.
questions.shortcut: $90 + \frac{60}{2} = 120^\circ$. Trap: $2A = 120^\circ$ happens to match here too, but the incentre formula is the safe route.

questions.q: In a housing society of **150 families, 90 have a car, 70 have a two-wheeler and 40 have both**. How many families have **neither**?
questions.solution: At least one = 90 + 70 − 40 = 120. Neither = 150 − 120 = **30**. 70 comes from 150 − (50 + 30), which forgets the 40 families who have both.

questions.q: **Imran walks 5 km North, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 9 km.** How far is he from the starting point?
questions.solution: North 5 → (0, 5); right = East 3 → (3, 5); right = South 9 → (3, −4). Distance = √(9 + 16) = **5 km**.
questions.shortcut: Components (3, 4) reappear after cancellation → the triple gives 5.
questions.pattern: shortest distance between start and finish
